title: Moqueca Baiana
subtitle: Bahian prawn and coconut milk stew with dende oil
excerpt: A rich, fragrant prawn stew from the state of Bahia, cooked with coconut milk, tomatoes and the earthy depth of dende oil. This is one of the most celebrated dishes in Brazilian cooking. It comes together in under an hour and is best eaten the same day.
sourceNotes: Moqueca baiana comes from the state of Bahia in northeastern Brazil, the heart of Afro-Brazilian culture. The dish blends indigenous Brazilian techniques with West African flavours brought by enslaved people, particularly the use of dende oil and coconut milk. It differs from the Espirito Santo version, which uses neither.

glossaryTerms.definition: Palm oil used in Bahian and West African cooking. It has a rich, earthy flavour and gives moqueca its distinctive orange colour. It is high in saturated fat and a small amount goes a long way.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and is ready in about 50 minutes. The stew is built in a single pan and comes together quickly once the base is ready, so it suits a relaxed midweek dinner as well as a weekend gathering. Serve it with white rice to soak up the broth.

. If you cannot find dende oil, substitute regular vegetable oil: the stew will be milder in flavour and pale rather than orange, but still good. Do not overcook the prawns; they need just 3 to 4 minutes in the hot liquid or they will turn rubbery.

content.text: Peel and devein 600g large raw prawns. Place them in a bowl with the lime juice, a pinch of salt and the coriander stalks, finely chopped. Toss well and set aside to marinate while you prepare the base.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wide, deep pan over medium heat. Add the onion rings and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and 1 sliced red pepper and 1 sliced green pepper and cook for another 3 minutes.

Layer the sliced tomatoes over the softened vegetables. Season with salt. Pour over the coconut milk and add the dende oil. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then cook for 10 minutes uncovered until the sauce has thickened slightly and the tomatoes have broken down.

Add the marinated prawns to the pan in a single layer, including any juices from the bowl. Cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the prawns are pink and just cooked through. Do not stir too much or they will overcook.
Taste and adjust the salt. Scatter over the coriander leaves and serve immediately with rice.

attrs.cause: Overcooked: prawns cook very fast and continue cooking from residual heat after the pan is off
attrs.fix: Cook prawns for no more than 4 minutes in the simmering liquid. Remove the pan from the heat as soon as they are pink all the way through.

attrs.cause: Tomatoes were very watery, or the coconut milk was low-fat
attrs.fix: Simmer uncovered for a further 10 minutes before adding the prawns to reduce the liquid. Use full-fat coconut milk for the best result.

attrs.cause: Dende oil can turn bitter if it scorches or is cooked over high heat for too long
attrs.fix: Always add dende oil to liquid that is already in the pan, not to a dry hot pan. Keep the heat at medium and avoid letting the sauce catch on the bottom.

content.text: Bahia is the state in northeastern Brazil with the strongest African culinary heritage, and moqueca baiana is its most famous dish. It is cooked in a clay pot called a panela de barro, which keeps the heat even and adds a subtle earthiness. Street restaurants in Salvador serve it all week, but it feels most at home on a Sunday with the smell of coconut drifting out of the kitchen.
